name: search-engine

ground_truth.threatName: Unauthorized Data Access via Kendra Search Results

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Without proper ACLs and user context in Kendra queries, the search service might return results containing sensitive information to unauthorized users.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: A malicious user could craft search queries that return documents they shouldn't have access to, bypassing intended access controls.

recommendations.description: Implement user-context aware search with Kendra
recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure Kendra index with UserContextPolicy and UserTokenConfigurations. Modify search service to include user context in every Kendra query. Implement document-level ACLs in S3 and reflect these in Kendra's data source configuration.

recommendations.description: Implement result filtering at application layer
recommendations.implementationDetails: Add post-query filtering in the search service to double-check access permissions before returning results to users.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS IAM for authentication and authorization. Implement S3 bucket policies and object-level ACLs. Configure Kendra's Principal Store to sync with your identity provider.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Cache keys might not properly incorporate user context, leading to information leakage between users. Additionally, cache invalidation issues could lead to stale or incorrect data being served.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could poison the cache with malicious data or access another user's cached search results by manipulating cache keys.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Include user ID or role in cache keys. Implement cache key hashing to prevent manipulation. Set appropriate TTL values for cached items.
Add version numbers to cached items. Implement cache invalidation on content updates. Add monitoring for cache hit/miss ratios and suspicious patterns.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS ElastiCache auth tokens and encryption in transit. Implement proper VPC security groups and network ACLs.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Without TLS, all API communications are sent in plaintext, making them vulnerable to interception and manipulation.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could perform man-in-the-middle attacks to intercept search queries and results, or manipulate API requests.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use AWS Certificate Manager to provision a certificate. Configure API Gateway with custom domain and TLS certificate. Force HTTPS-only communication.
Add security headers including HSTS, CSP, etc. Configure minimum TLS version (1.2+).

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS ACM for certificate management. Configure security policies in API Gateway. Enable AWS Shield for DDoS protection.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Without proper token refresh mechanisms and expiration policies, compromised tokens could be used for extended periods.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who obtains a valid token could maintain access indefinitely if tokens don't expire or require refresh.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use short-lived access tokens with refresh tokens. Implement token rotation. Add token revocation capabilities.
Add token fingerprinting. Implement device binding. Monitor for suspicious token usage patterns.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Consider using Amazon Cognito for token management. Implement AWS WAF rules to detect token abuse patterns.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could manipulate the search service or API handlers to make requests to internal services or metadata endpoints.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could craft a search query that causes the service to make requests to internal endpoints or AWS metadata service.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Validate and sanitize all URLs. Implement allowlist for permitted domains/IPs. Block access to link-local and private IP ranges.
Configure IMDSv2 on EC2 instances. Implement strict security groups and NACLs. Use VPC endpoints for AWS services.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS SecurityHub for security monitoring. Implement VPC endpoints with strict policies. Enable IMDSv2 requirement flag.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Internal service communications without TLS could be intercepted within the VPC, especially in a compromised network scenario.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker who gains access to the VPC network could intercept communications between Kendra and its data sources.

recommendations.description: Enable TLS for all internal communications
recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure TLS for all service-to-service communication. Use AWS Private Certificate Authority for internal certificates.
Deploy VPC Flow Logs. Enable AWS Network Firewall. Monitor for unencrypted traffic.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Private Certificate Authority for internal PKI. Implement VPC endpoints with TLS enforcement. Enable encryption in transit for all supported services.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
AWS Scalable Search Engine Architecture Diagram
This diagram illustrates a scalable search system using various AWS services,
including authentication, API management, search functionality, and data storage components.
"""

# Network and Security imports
from diagrams.aws.network import APIGateway, ELB
from diagrams.aws.security import IAM

# Compute imports
from diagrams.aws.compute import Lambda, ECS, ElasticBeanstalk

# Database and Storage imports
from diagrams.aws.database import Dynamodb, ElasticacheForRedis, RDS
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3

# Analytics and Search imports
from diagrams.aws.ml import Rekognition as Kendra  # Using Rekognition icon as a substitute for Kendra
from diagrams.aws.integration import SimpleQueueServiceSqs

# Management and Monitoring imports
from diagrams.aws.management import Cloudwatch, AutoScaling

# General diagram components
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge
from diagrams.generic.device import Mobile

# Diagram configuration
graph_attr = {
    "fontsize": "45",
    "bgcolor": "white",
    "splines": "spline",
    "pad": "2.0",
    "nodesep": "0.60",
    "ranksep": "0.75"
}

# Create the diagram with custom configuration
with Diagram(
    "AWS Scalable Search Engine",
    filename="search_engine",
    show=False,
    direction="LR",
    graph_attr=graph_attr,
    outformat="png"
) as diag:
    
    # Define client/user (outside AWS account)
    users = Mobile("Users")
    
    # AWS Account boundary
    with Cluster("AWS Account"):
        # Security and API Management cluster
        with Cluster("Security & API Layer"):
            iam = IAM("Authentication")
            api = APIGateway("API Gateway")
            load_balancer = ELB("Load Balancer")
        
        # Application Services cluster
        with Cluster("Search Services"):
            api_handlers = Lambda("API Handlers")
            search_service = ECS("Search Service")
            indexer = Lambda("Data Indexer")
            with Cluster("Auto Scaling Group"):
                search_workers = [
                    ElasticBeanstalk("Search Worker 1"),
                    ElasticBeanstalk("Search Worker 2")
                ]
        
        # Intelligent Search and Cache cluster
        with Cluster("Intelligent Search & Cache"):
            kendra = Kendra("Amazon Kendra")
            cache = ElasticacheForRedis("Results Cache")
        
        # Data Storage cluster
        with Cluster("Data Layer"):
            document_store = S3("Document Store")
            metadata_db = Dynamodb("Metadata Store")
            content_db = RDS("Content Database")
        
        # Queue System
        index_queue = SimpleQueueServiceSqs("Indexing Queue")
        
        # Management & Monitoring
        with Cluster("Management"):
            monitoring = Cloudwatch("Monitoring")
            scaling = AutoScaling("Auto Scaling")
    
    # Define relationships with custom edges
    # User authentication flow
    users >> Edge(color="blue", label="1. HTTPS Request") >> api
    api >> Edge(color="green", label="2. Authenticate") >> iam
    iam >> Edge(color="green", label="3. Validate Token") >> api
    api >> Edge(color="darkgreen", label="4. Route Request") >> load_balancer
    
    # Search request flow
    load_balancer >> Edge(color="darkgreen", label="5. Forward") >> api_handlers
    api_handlers >> Edge(color="purple", label="6. Search Request") >> search_service
    
    # Search and result flow
    search_service >> Edge(color="red", label="7. Query") >> kendra
    kendra >> Edge(color="red", label="8. Search Results") >> search_service
    search_service >> Edge(color="orange", label="9a. Cache Results") >> cache
    cache >> Edge(color="orange", label="9b. Get Cached Results") >> search_service
    
    # Return results to user
    search_service >> Edge(color="purple", label="10. Results") >> api_handlers
    api_handlers >> Edge(color="blue", label="11. Format Response") >> api
    api >> Edge(color="blue", label="12. Return Results") >> users
    
    # Worker operations
    for worker in search_workers:
        search_service >> worker
        worker >> kendra
    
    # Data indexing flow
    indexer >> Edge(color="blue", label="Index Content") >> kendra
    indexer >> Edge(color="blue", label="Fetch Documents") >> document_store
    index_queue >> Edge(color="orange", label="Trigger") >> indexer
    
    # Database interactions
    search_service >> Edge(color="purple", label="Metadata") >> metadata_db
    search_service >> Edge(color="purple", label="Content") >> content_db
    
    # Monitoring and scaling
    [api_handlers, search_service, kendra] >> monitoring
    scaling >> Edge(color="red", label="Scale") >> search_workers
    
    # Performance optimization
    kendra >> Edge(color="orange", label="Cache Results") >> cache
    search_service >> Edge(color="orange", label="Check Cache") >> cache

# Note: The diagram will be saved as 'search_engine.png' in high resolution
